review_type: AI editorial review of A2 speaking tasks in the four official DUO types (video-answer, picture-describe, picture-choose, picture-sequence) and their sentence starters: prompt shape and official instruction wording, cues and voice roles, image briefs against the house style and cast, criteria that mirror the type, sample quotes, model coverage, level, originality

Focused re-review of 10 September 2026: the two required edits and five recommended edits were applied exactly as requested and nothing else changed; 24 pass at source hash e40eadfb. Starters pass at their unchanged hash. Ready for integration.

checks.prompt_wording_note: video-answer prompts say 'U hoort de vraag. Geef antwoord.' after '... stelt u een vraag.'; blueprint 4.3 records 'U hoort een vraag.'; accepted, the coordinator decides which pattern the blueprint records

starters_checks.notes: Five starters end in a fronted adverbial and leave the inversion to the learner ('s Nachts ...; Op het andere plaatje ... in flat-dorp and sportschool-park; Op het derde plaatje ... in rijbewijs; Bij de kleermaker ...). Accepted as in the 008 review; optional safer fragments: ''s Nachts slaap ik ...', 'Op het andere plaatje zie ik ...', 'Op het derde plaatje is hij ...', 'Bij de kleermaker laat hij ...'. Applying them moves the starters hash and needs a focused re-review.

items.evidence: Video-answer, werk. Prompt gives the situation then 'U hoort de vraag. Geef antwoord.'; cue by Julio (m-young), 20 words, one two-part question (ochtend of avond, en waarom), informal jij from a colleague. Quotes 'Ik werk liever in de avond.' and 'Dan is het rustig op het werk.' are exact; the sample adds no further detail, so criterion 3 is null. Model 33 words meets all three (ochtend; fris and sneller; om zeven uur), one als-clause. Still: Julio with the exact cast traits; the brief asks for 'a paper calendar', an object made of printed numbers, so its 'No text' cannot be honoured.
items.level_check: comparable: a direct two-part question about a work preference, answered in three or four short sentences.
items.revision_request: images[0].brief: replace with 'Julio (young man, curly hair, striped shirt) sits at an office desk with a laptop and a few blank sheets of paper and turns towards the viewer as if asking a question. No text.' Alt text unchanged.
items.re_review: Focused re-review 2026-09-10: images[0].brief now reads exactly the requested replacement (a few blank sheets of paper instead of a paper calendar); cast traits verbatim, No text clause honourable, alt unchanged and still accurate. Pass.

items.evidence: Video-answer, opleiding. Cue by the teacher (f-adult), 17 words, u-register, two parts (hoe, hoe vaak). Quotes for how and for 'Zo leer ik nieuwe woorden.' are exact; no frequency, so criterion 2 is null. Model 36 words: tv news and the neighbour, 'bijna elke dag, een half uur', a reason. Still: a non-cast teacher with three traits beside a blank whiteboard.
items.level_check: comparable: a personal two-part question with everyday vocabulary.

items.evidence: Video-answer, wonen-buurt. Cue by mevrouw Bakker (f-older), 21 words, two parts (hoe lang, wat vindt u). 'Welkom in de straat!' is no criterion; quotes 2 and 3 exact; no duration, so criterion 1 is null. Model 33 words in six short sentences meets all three. Still: mevrouw Bakker with exact traits and a moving box at a low fence.
items.level_check: comparable: opinion about one's own street with a duration and details.

items.evidence: Video-answer, gezondheid. Cue by the huisarts (m-older; the role lists huisarts), 20 words, two clock-time questions. Quotes 1 and 3 exact; no rising time, so criterion 2 is null. Model 33 words: twaalf uur, zes uur op with a reason, six hours of sleep, waking at night. Still: non-cast doctor with three traits, stethoscope, no white coat, no screen. Nothing graphic; the times are role-play facts.

items.evidence: Video-answer, winkels-diensten. Cue by the shop employee (m-shop), 16 words, abonnement of prepaidkaart plus internet use. The sample never names either product, so criterion 1 is null; quotes 2 and 3 (two contiguous sentences) exact. Model 33 words: abonnement, veel internet with video calls as reason, music and a price question. Still: non-cast employee with three traits, plain phones, no text or logos. Phone-shop overlap with the repair items is setting only; the act is new and on the needed list.
items.level_check: comparable: a product choice and a yes/no with a reason; abonnement and prepaidkaart are everyday in this situation.
items.recommended_edit: model: 'Ik luister ook veel muziek op mijn telefoon.' -> 'Ik luister ook veel naar muziek op mijn telefoon.' (not blocking)

items.evidence: Video-answer, vervoer. Cue by meneer De Vries (m-older), 18 words, which bus and how often. Quotes 1 and 3 exact; no frequency, so criterion 2 is null. Model 27 words: lijn vier, elk kwartier, the stop across the road, ten minutes. Still: meneer De Vries with exact traits at a simple bus stop. The learner invents the line number; any line and frequency satisfy the criteria (doubt 7 accepted).

doubts_answered.12_rijbewijs_pink_card: Keep the card (unambiguous outcome); handshake fallback only if unreadable at display size; note the procedural shortcut in the image review.

diversity_review: Twenty-four distinct settings and acts across the four official types and all eight A2 domains (three each); no slug reuse; no re-skin of a catalogue speaking item (all eleven are three-point voicemail messages) or of a blueprint 9 setting; only the fixed instruction sentences mirror the official format and no official scenario is reused. Near pairs accepted with reasons: abonnement vs the phone-shop repair items (different act and part); afval vs batch003-container and the KNM gft card (different act); paspoort and brief-gemeente (both at the gemeente; different drills); thuis-oefenen and klas-thuis (habits vs preference; different types); nieuwe-buurvrouw vs the buurvrouw voicemail; bushalte vs tramkaart (giving vs asking help); verjaardag and trein-auto share only a birthday motif. Julio, Karim, Fatima and mevrouw Bakker appear three times each; consecutive tasks in a form should not reuse a name.

set_assembly.rule: drill = four tasks of one type; mock form = 4+4+4+4; six per type gives one form plus one half form (2+2+2+2) with no shared items

proposed_mock_form.properties: every domain exactly twice, no cue voice twice, no cast name in consecutive tasks, the two gemeente sequences separated

cautions: slaap and bushalte share the m-older voice (different characters); keep them apart in a video drill or accept
paspoort and brief-gemeente do not share a drill
gymles enters a set only after its revision
the launch bank of twelve per type needs one more batch of this shape before two mocks without shared items exist

image_risks: text-bearing objects: bus-stop pole (bushalte), phone display (abonnement), container pictograms (afval), book spines (kringloop), shop fronts and tram (flat-dorp), form and passport (paspoort), tickets and popcorn bucket (bioscoop), pink card (rijbewijs)
small details: candles and ribbons (verjaardag), rope (gymles), stethoscope (slaap), measuring tape and pins (kleermaker), cones (rijbewijs)

consistency: the friend in bioscoop, the suitcase in vakantie, the present in trein-auto, sports clothing of Sem and mevrouw Bakker (cast rule), Karim's jacket at the campsite
alt texts are neutral and, for describe tasks, name the pictured objects, which is right for an open task

limitations: This is an AI editorial review. It does not replace independent Dutch-language educator review, learner trials, blueprint validation or psychometric calibration, and it does not establish equivalence with an official exam.
The A2 labels remain unvalidated authoring targets; the per-task level judgments compare the tasks with the official task descriptions, not with stored exemplars or learner data.

The approval of the twenty-two passing tasks applies only to the exact source and starter hashes recorded here; any byte change requires a new hash and a focused re-review.
